newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt portfolios less bullish Dec 3 wk -survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt portfolios less bullish Dec 3 wk -survey.

text.p: Money managers pared duration exposure on their U.S. debt portfolios in the past week, signaling a less bullish outlook, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
After seven consecutive weeks of seeing most survey participants extend duration exposure, "this week finally saw a very small pullback," the report said.
"The arithmetic measure of duration exposure dipped to 102.1 from 102.5," it said.

In the week ended December 3, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading fell to 4.89 from 5.14 the prior week; the asset-weighted number slipped to 4.64 from 4.77 in the week ended November 26, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 6.45 percent from 6.57 percent.
Duration bogey rose to 4.22 on an arithmetic basis and rose to 4.93 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 16 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.0, down from 5.75 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
